title: IdleWorlds : music producer branching into web, oldschool text-based MMORPG gamedev assisted by AI - community growing fast, 100% free-to-play,
author: matduke
selftext:
Hey everyone! I want to show you the game I’ve been building with AI: IdleWorlds.  
  
[https://idleworlds.com](https://idleworlds.com)

It’s a free browser/mobile MMORPG. Text-based, incremental, idle-focused. You choose an action — mining, combat, herb gathering, potion brewing, crafting — and your character keeps progressing server-side every 10 seconds, even when the game is closed.

The whole idea is:  
log out → sleep → wake up → open your bags → dopamine 😂

The AI angle

The game started from an AI prompt around 2 months ago. But honestly the original version was basically nothing compared to what exists now. The AI gave me a starting point. Since then it’s been countless hours of debugging, balancing, designing systems, rewriting stuff, listening to player feedback, promoting the game, handling servers, and actively playing my own game.

People sometimes say things like “AI slop” instantly when they hear AI was involved, but from my perspective AI is what finally allowed me to make the kind of game I always wanted to make. I’m a music producer originally (18+ years, 100+ released songs) so I’ve always been creative, but coding a full MMORPG solo would have been impossible for me a few years ago.

Now I can actually build.

And honestly? It’s addictive. Not just the game — the process itself. Waking up with ideas, implementing systems in real-time, pushing updates instantly, watching players discover mechanics, fixing bugs live while people are online. It feels like indie game development got unlocked for a whole new category of people.

The actual game

The game already has:

* 6 skills: combat, mining, smithing, herbalism, alchemy, and the newest one: Jewelcrafting
* Hourly world bosses Everyone attacks together asynchronously and everyone gets the server buff if it dies.
* Zone Control Optional async PvP/team territory system with monthly resets.
* Active player market Listings + buy orders.
* Dungeon progression
* Mail system
* Gear upgrading
* Rare drop announcements in chat
* Multiple visual themes (including an “office mode” skin because yes people literally play this at work 😂)

One thing players seem to really love is the fallback system. If your character runs out of materials while offline, it intelligently falls back to previous activities instead of just stopping completely.

The community part surprised me the most

This is probably my favorite thing so far.

The game isn’t even 2 months old and somehow the community already feels like old-school internet gaming. Players help each other, gift gear to newbies, explain mechanics, discuss economy opportunities, etc.

I intentionally leave some things slightly obscure instead of over-explaining every mechanic instantly. Kind of inspired by older MMOs where discovering stuff with other players was part of the fun.

Monetization

The game is genuinely F2P.

Right now monetization is basically:

* cosmetic name colors
* chat badges
* small QoL support perks

There’s no “buy power” stuff because I personally hate hyper-P2W gacha design. I’m building the kind of forever-sidegame I’d actually want to play myself. Something chill you can manage while working, gaming, raising kids, whatever.

Recently added

This week I added Jewelcrafting, which completely changed the economy. Players can now prospect ore for gems and craft jewelry. Lower-level ores stay relevant because they still contain useful gem opportunities, which keeps early zones alive economically.

Honestly seeing players discover profitable strategies before I even fully understand the meta myself has been one of the coolest parts of building this game 😂

Biggest thing I learned building with AI

AI is insanely good at helping you START things.

But making something people actually stick around for still comes down to:

* game feel
* progression pacing
* economy balance
* community
* retention
* constant iteration
* taste

That part still feels very human.

Anyway, if anyone here is also building AI-assisted games, I’d genuinely love to hear what your experience has been like. I feel like we’re entering a super weird/fun era for indie dev.

And if you want to check out IdleWorlds yourself, I’d love more feedback from fellow AI game dev people.

Thanks for reading 🙏  
:::
